messages.subject: path analysis with binary variables
parts:
Hey everyone,

I'm trying to run a path analysis (no latent variables) using lavaan. My model looks like this:

mymodel<-'SuicideIdeation_dich ~ f3_24 + YSFISOFR + PDDQ_mean + scl27_gsi 
                 f3_24 ~ StigmaThreat_mean + StigmaCopingRes_mean + GroupId_mean + scl27_gsi
                 f3_24 ~~ YSFISOFR
                 YSFISOFR ~ StigmaThreat_mean + StigmaCopingRes_mean + GroupId_mean + scl27_gsi 
                 StigmaThreat_mean ~ PDDQ_mean + GroupId_mean 
                 StigmaThreat_mean ~~ StigmaCopingRes_mean
                 StigmaCopingRes_mean ~ PDDQ_mean '

fit<-sem(mymodel, data=TP1dataDepr, ordered=c("f3_24", "YSFISOFR", "SuicideIdeation_dich"))
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)


SuicideIIdeation_dich is my main outcome and is dichotomous (high=1, low=0).


As far as I understood R is using DWLS, instead of ML, and the results are interpreted similar to probit regression.


My question is:
- which fit indices should I consider (Chi-square, RMSEA and CFI all look fine)
- R is presenting estimates and  standardized estimates (std.all), which one should I use?
- Do you know a publication which used the same approach, so I could get a feeling for how to do this correctly (I'm a Master student with no experience in path analysis)

Thanks a lot!

Nathalie

On 02/20/2015 10:37 AM, Nathalie Oexle wrote:
> As far as I understood R is using DWLS, instead of ML, and the results
> are interpreted similar to probit regression.

> My question is:
> - which fit indices should I consider (Chi-square, RMSEA and CFI all
> look fine)

In the summary() output, you will get two columns. You need to look at
the second column ('Robust').

> - R is presenting estimates and standardized estimates (std.all), which
> one should I use?
Both are useful. It depends if you prefer raw or standardized estimates.

> - Do you know a publication which used the same approach, so I could get
> a feeling for how to do this correctly (I'm a Master student with no
> experience in path analysis)

I think if you google around a bit, you will find plenty.

Yves.
